title: Paul Before Festus, Paul Appeals to Caesar

questions.question: When Festus arrived in Caesarea, the chief priests and Jewish leaders requested that Paul be sent to Jerusalem — why?
options: They were planning an ambush to kill him along the way
They wanted to try him under Jewish law in Jerusalem
They expected Festus to find him guilty and condemn him
They wanted to question him before the Sanhedrin formally
questions.correctAnswer: They were planning an ambush to kill him along the way
questions.explanation: Acts 25:3 (ESV): "They were asking him, as a favor against Paul, to summon him to Jerusalem—because they were planning an ambush to kill him on the way."

questions.question: When Festus asked Paul if he wished to go to Jerusalem to be tried, what did Paul respond?
options: "I am standing before Caesar's tribunal, where I ought to be tried... I appeal to Caesar."
"No, I demand a fair trial before you here in Caesarea."
"I refuse to return to Jerusalem where my life is at risk."
"I am a Roman citizen and insist on being tried in Rome."
questions.correctAnswer: "I am standing before Caesar's tribunal, where I ought to be tried... I appeal to Caesar."
questions.explanation: Acts 25:10-11 (ESV): "Then Paul said, 'I am standing before Caesar's tribunal, where I ought to be tried...I appeal to Caesar.'"

questions.question: After Paul's appeal to Caesar, Festus conferred with his council. What was his response?
options: "You have appealed to Caesar; to Caesar you shall go."
"Your appeal is granted; await transport to Rome."
"I will send you to Caesar as you have requested."
"The appeal is received; preparations will be made."
questions.correctAnswer: "You have appealed to Caesar; to Caesar you shall go."
questions.explanation: Acts 25:12 (ESV): "Then Festus, when he had conferred with his council, answered, 'You have appealed to Caesar; to Caesar you shall go.'"

questions.question: King Agrippa came to Caesarea with Bernice to welcome Festus. Festus shared Paul's case. What was Agrippa's response?
options: "I would like to hear the man myself." And the next day Agrippa heard him.
"Send him to Caesar as he requested, without delay."
"Bring him before me in private first, then we shall decide."
"The man should be freed; I see no charge against him."
questions.correctAnswer: "I would like to hear the man myself." And the next day Agrippa heard him.
questions.explanation: Acts 25:22 (ESV): "Then Agrippa said to Festus, 'I would like to hear the man myself.' 'Tomorrow,' said he, 'you will hear him.'"

questions.question: Festus explained to Agrippa his difficulty with Paul's case: he had nothing definite to write to Caesar about. The charges were about their own religion and about "a certain Jesus, who was dead, but whom Paul asserted to be..."?
options: alive
the Christ
the Son of God
risen from the dead
questions.explanation: Acts 25:19 (ESV): "Rather they had certain points of dispute with him about their own religion and about a certain Jesus, who was dead, but whom Paul asserted to be alive."

questions.question: Paul told Festus he had done wrong to no one — neither to "the Jews, nor to the temple, nor to..."?
options: Caesar
the law
Rome
God
questions.explanation: Acts 25:8 (ESV): "Paul argued in his defense, 'Neither against the law of the Jews, nor against the temple, nor against Caesar have I committed any offense.'"

questions.question: Festus described Paul's opponents as not charging him with crimes he expected but disputed about what?
options: Questions about their own religion and about whether a dead man, Jesus, was alive
Whether Paul had broken Roman law while in Asia Minor
Whether Paul had deliberately caused riots in Jerusalem
Whether Paul's teaching undermined loyalty to the Roman empire
questions.correctAnswer: Questions about their own religion and about whether a dead man, Jesus, was alive
questions.explanation: Acts 25:19 (ESV): "Rather they had certain points of dispute with him about their own religion and about a certain Jesus, who was dead, but whom Paul asserted to be alive."

questions.question: Festus entered the audience hall with Agrippa and Bernice and with what kind of display?
options: With great pomp, with military tribunes and the prominent men of the city
With the full Sanhedrin present as witnesses to the proceedings
With a procession of priests both Jewish and pagan from Caesarea
With Roman legates sent from Rome to assist with the trial
questions.correctAnswer: With great pomp, with military tribunes and the prominent men of the city
questions.explanation: Acts 25:23 (ESV): "So on the next day Agrippa and Bernice came with great pomp, and they entered the audience hall with the military tribunes and the prominent men of the city."

questions.question: Festus said Paul had done nothing deserving death but had appealed to Caesar. He said he wanted to write something reasonable about Paul to send. What did he need?
options: Something definite to charge him with — he had nothing clear to write to his lord (Caesar)
Paul's cooperation in answering the Jewish charges formally
A summary from Agrippa who was expert in Jewish matters
The official verdict of the Sanhedrin in written form
questions.correctAnswer: Something definite to charge him with — he had nothing clear to write to his lord (Caesar)
questions.explanation: Acts 25:26 (ESV): "But I have nothing definite to write to my lord about him. Therefore I have brought him before you all, and especially before you, King Agrippa, so that, after we have examined him, I may have something to write."

questions.question: Paul said it was unreasonable for him to grant the Jews a favor by going to Jerusalem to be tried there, where he had actually done no wrong. He argued that if he was guilty of something worthy of death he would not refuse to die. But if their charges were false, no one could simply "deliver him" to what?
options: Them — as a favor
Death — without proper process
Jerusalem — away from Caesar's court
The Jewish council — without Roman authorization
questions.explanation: Acts 25:11 (ESV): "If then I am a wrongdoer and have committed anything for which I deserve to die, I do not seek to escape death. But if there is nothing to their charges against me, no one can give me up to them. I appeal to Caesar."

questions.question: Festus came to Jerusalem first after arriving in the province of Judea. After only how many days did he go down to Caesarea?
options: Eight or ten days
Three days
Fourteen days
Twenty days
questions.explanation: Acts 25:1,6 (ESV): "Now three days after Festus had arrived in the province, he went up to Jerusalem... After he stayed among them not more than eight or ten days, he went down to Caesarea."

questions.question: What was Festus willing to do as a favor to the Jews, which Paul refused?
options: Go to Jerusalem and be tried before Festus there
Submit to a trial before the Sanhedrin in Jerusalem
Face his accusers before Jewish law without Roman protection
Allow the Jewish high priest to determine his guilt or innocence
questions.correctAnswer: Go to Jerusalem and be tried before Festus there
questions.explanation: Acts 25:9 (ESV): "But Festus, wishing to do the Jews a favor, said to Paul, 'Do you wish to go up to Jerusalem and there be tried on these charges before me?'"

questions.question: Festus emphasized to Agrippa that it seemed unreasonable to him to send a prisoner without what?
options: Indicating the charges against him
A formal Roman trial first
Written testimony from witnesses
The official seal of the Sanhedrin
questions.explanation: Acts 25:27 (ESV): "For it seems to me unreasonable, in sending a prisoner, not to indicate the charges against him."

questions.question: Bernice appears with Agrippa throughout this chapter. What was their relationship?
options: Sister and brother (Agrippa II and his sister Bernice)
King and his royal wife from the Herodian line
Father and daughter of the Herodian dynasty
Uncle and niece connected through Herod Agrippa I
questions.correctAnswer: Sister and brother (Agrippa II and his sister Bernice)
questions.explanation: Acts 25:13,23 reference Agrippa and Bernice together; historically they were brother and sister (children of Herod Agrippa I).

questions.question: Why did Festus not directly send Paul to Caesar immediately when Paul appealed?
options: He needed something definite to write about the charges
He first needed permission from Agrippa as a local king
He wanted to ensure Paul was in good health for the voyage
He needed to gather witnesses who could testify in Rome
questions.correctAnswer: He needed something definite to write about the charges
questions.explanation: Acts 25:26-27 (ESV): "But I have nothing definite to write to my lord about him... it seems unreasonable, in sending a prisoner, not to indicate the charges against him."
